title: Finite limits and finite colimits
statement: A category $\mathcal I$ is *finite* if it has finitely many objects and finitely many morphisms; a *finite limit* (resp. *finite colimit*) in a category $\mathcal C$ is a limit (resp. colimit) of a diagram $M:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ indexed by a finite category $\mathcal I$. The category $\mathcal C$ *has finite limits* (resp. *has finite colimits*) if every diagram $M:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ with $\mathcal I$ finite has a limit (resp. a colimit) in $\mathcal C$.
